newsitem.title: USA: White House aide sees China MFN renewal.
newsitem.headline: White House aide sees China MFN renewal.

text.p: White House legislative director John Hilley said Wednesday he expects President Clinton to seek renewal of China's Most Favored Nation Trade status and Congress to accept it after a tough debate.
"Every year it's a fight and we have to work it hard," Hilley told a small group of reporters. "I see that one coming out, I hope, like last year."

China's trade status is reviewed annually by lawmakers. Clinton has until June to decide on MFN, which allows Chinese goods into the country at the same low tariff rates as goods from almost all other countries. Congress then has to decide whether to overturn that decision.

After a sometimes emotional debate about human rights, nuclear technology proliferation and the huge U.S. trade deficit with China, Congress failed to overturn Clinton's decision to renew MFN last year. The business community strongly supports China's MFN status and has urged an end to the annual review ritual.
